paragraphs.title: Personal Thanks for the Lord’s Kindness

answers: With his whole heart
Only in secret
Through the kings of the earth
easy.explanation: The speaker says, “I will praise thee with my whole heart.”
easy.q: How does the speaker praise the Lord?

answers: The enemies’ camp
The Lord’s holy temple
The kings’ throne
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will worship toward thy holy temple.”
easy.q: Toward what does the speaker worship?

answers: For His lovingkindness and truth
For his own wealth
For the strength of his enemies
easy.explanation: The speaker praises the Lord’s name for His “lovingkindness” and “truth.”
easy.q: For what does the speaker praise the Lord’s name?

answers: The Lord answered him and strengthened him
The kings sang before him
He left the holy temple
medium.explanation: The speaker says, “In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me.”
medium.q: What happened when the speaker cried to the Lord?

answers: The Lord weakened his spirit
The Lord gave him inward strength
The Lord removed him from worship
medium.explanation: The phrase describes strength given to the speaker within his soul.
medium.q: What does “strengthenedst me with strength in my soul” mean?

answers: The speaker expresses both reverence and thanksgiving to the Lord
The speaker worships in order to hide his praise
The speaker praises only after leaving the temple
medium.explanation: He worships toward the holy temple and praises the Lord’s name for His kindness and truth.
medium.q: How are worship and praise connected in these verses?

answers: Praise offered only during trouble
Complete and sincere praise
Praise belonging only to kings
challenge.explanation: “With my whole heart” emphasizes wholehearted and sincere devotion.
challenge.q: What does “with my whole heart” emphasize?

answers: The speaker praises the Lord openly in His presence
The speaker opposes everything the Lord says
The speaker sings only before human beings
challenge.explanation: The speaker declares that he will sing praise to the Lord openly before the gods.
challenge.q: What does “before the gods will I sing praise unto thee” show?

answers: The speaker forgot the Lord’s words
The Lord’s word is shown to be exceedingly great and trustworthy
The speaker’s name is greater than the Lord’s name
challenge.explanation: The verse magnifies the greatness and reliability of the Lord’s word.
challenge.q: What is meant by “thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name”?

short_answers.question: What two qualities of the Lord are mentioned in verse 2?
short_answers.explanation: The speaker praises the Lord’s name for His “lovingkindness” and “truth.”

paragraphs.title: The Kings’ Acknowledgment and the Lord’s Greatness

answers: All the kings of the earth
Only the speaker
Only the temple servants
easy.explanation: The verse says, “All the kings of the earth shall praise thee, O LORD.”

answers: The songs of their enemies
The words of the Lord’s mouth
Only the speaker’s words
easy.explanation: The kings will praise the Lord when they hear “the words of thy mouth.”

answers: The ways of the Lord
Their own riches
Their military power
easy.explanation: The verse says, “they shall sing in the ways of the LORD.”
easy.q: What will the kings sing about?

answers: They see the holy temple
They hear the words of the Lord’s mouth
They defeat their enemies
medium.explanation: Their praise follows when they hear the Lord’s words.
medium.q: What causes the kings to praise and sing?

answers: Humble or socially insignificant
Someone who is merely far away
Someone who boasts over others
medium.explanation: The lowly are those who are humble or of low position.
medium.q: What does “lowly” mean in this passage?

answers: He is high, yet regards the lowly
He is distant and knows no one
He reveals Himself only to kings
medium.explanation: Although the Lord is high, He still has respect unto the lowly.
medium.q: How is the Lord’s greatness described?

answers: The Lord is exalted but attentive to humble people
The Lord is lower than humanity
The lowly are unworthy of the Lord’s attention
challenge.explanation: The contrast emphasizes the Lord’s greatness and His care for the humble.
challenge.q: What contrast is presented between “high” and “lowly”?

answers: The Lord cannot notice proud people
The Lord recognizes the proud even from a distance
The proud draw near to the Lord in humility
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Lord knows or recognizes the proud from afar.
challenge.q: What does “the proud he knoweth afar off” mean?

answers: The kings hear the Lord’s words, praise Him, and sing of His ways
The kings fight, win, and then withdraw
The kings hide, become silent, and leave
challenge.explanation: Hearing the Lord’s words leads the kings to praise and sing in His ways.
challenge.q: What sequence is described in verses 4–5?

short_answers.question: What will the kings of the earth do when they hear the Lord’s words?
short_answers.answer: They will praise the Lord and sing in His ways.
short_answers.explanation: Verses 4–5 connect hearing the Lord’s words with praise and singing.

paragraphs.title: Deliverance in Trouble and Trust in Everlasting Kindness

answers: Revive him
Abandon him
Deliver him to his enemies
easy.explanation: The speaker says, “Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me.”
easy.q: What will the Lord do when the speaker walks through trouble?

answers: Stretch forth His hand and save him
Praise the enemies
Ignore them completely
easy.explanation: The Lord will stretch forth His hand, and His right hand shall save the speaker.
easy.q: What will the Lord do against the speaker’s enemies?

answers: Only until the trouble ends
For one day
For ever
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever.”
easy.q: How long does the Lord’s mercy endure?

answers: The Lord revives the speaker, acts against his enemies, and saves him
The Lord withdraws, remains silent, and yields to the enemies
The Lord sends enemies, strengthens them, and hides His hand
medium.explanation: The verse describes revival in trouble, the Lord’s hand against enemies, and salvation.
medium.q: What sequence of actions is described in verse 7?

answers: Do not abandon
Do not sing
Do not see
medium.explanation: The speaker asks the Lord not to abandon the works of His own hands.

answers: Because the Lord’s mercy endures for ever
Because the speaker is himself a king
Because all his enemies have already disappeared
medium.explanation: The speaker’s confidence rests on the Lord’s everlasting mercy.
medium.q: Why can the speaker trust in the Lord’s help?

answers: The Lord will complete what concerns the speaker and will not abandon His work
The Lord will stop answering the speaker
The speaker will give up his request
challenge.explanation: The speaker trusts the Lord to complete His work concerning him.
challenge.q: What does “The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me” express?

answers: The speaker depends only on his own strength in trouble
In trouble, the speaker trusts the Lord’s revival, salvation, and everlasting mercy
Mercy lasts only while there are no enemies
challenge.explanation: Even in trouble, the speaker relies on the Lord’s saving power and enduring mercy.
challenge.q: How do verses 7–8 connect trouble with mercy?

answers: The speaker sees himself as someone made and cared for by the Lord
The speaker claims to have created the Lord
The speaker wants to avoid all of the Lord’s work
challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses dependence on the Lord as Creator and protector.
challenge.q: What does “the works of thine own hands” imply about the speaker?

short_answers.question: What does the speaker ask the Lord not to do?
short_answers.answer: He asks the Lord not to forsake the works of His own hands.
short_answers.explanation: The psalm closes with the plea, “forsake not the works of thine own hands.”
